role: Character brand director — long-term recognition and distinctive brand behavior
stage: Independent concept note saved before reading Brand A; unbuilt cameo variation

evidence.inspection: Actual image viewed. Foreground coding moth, bench and MacBook dominate; workshop and resting moth already create two supporting story areas. Tree, winding path, flowers, bridge, tools, books and mug make the scene richly occupied.

Actual reference viewed. Anthropomorphic symbols and bright product-like forms are the central foreground cast around a picnic basket. Borrowing its warmth is compatible; importing its foreground cast hierarchy is incompatible. Product identities are not assumed.
Read in full, including latest foreground exclusion.
Read in full; relevant prior full skill intake reused.

independentRecommendation.scope: One bounded two-cameo study compared with the unchanged zero-cameo baseline. This is permission to test a concept, not approval of artwork or publication.
independentRecommendation.fit: Potentially fits as a small hint of the tools and company around Nag. The moth remains the author; cameos must not become the source of the banner's identity or a permanent requirement of heyNag.com.
independentRecommendation.positioning: One compact group in the deeper workshop/tree plane, behind the workshop and clearly separated from the resting moth at the large near tree. Keep the entire foreground bench, coder, MacBook and surrounding foreground path free of companions. Do not distribute two figures to opposite ends of the banner.
independentRecommendation.scale: Start each cameo around one third to one half the workshop moth's height, and below one fifth the foreground moth's height. These are trial proportions, not verified pixel requirements. Their combined colour mass must stay subordinate to the workshop moth; avoid bright isolated logo tiles.
independentRecommendation.story: A quiet pair near the workshop: one notices the moth building while the other lightly engages with the same small activity or a nearby leaf. They occupy one secondary moment rather than becoming a row of spectators admiring the foreground coder. Preserve the builder, coder and resting moth as three expressions of the same person.

otherCounts.0: Valid fallback and baseline; current art already tells the intended story.
otherCounts.3: Do not start here: a workshop watcher plus two tree players creates another separate story area before two cameos have earned their space.
otherCounts.full: Reject for this composition: the reference's central product ensemble would overwhelm personal authorship and long-term independence from particular tools.

failureCriteria: Any companion enters, touches or overlaps the foreground bench/coder/MacBook zone or its surrounding foreground path.
The pair creates a fourth equally assertive focal area, occludes an existing moth action, or makes the resting moth look like a member of a product mascot cast.
At actual desktop banner size, bright companion shapes or recognizable symbols lead the composition ahead of the coding moth and its work.

At phone size, the added shapes become visual debris or can only be made intelligible by enlarging them into foreground competitors. Quiet disappearance at that size is preferable to forced logo recognition.
The concept only feels distinctive because viewers can name the external products. Remove cameos rather than making vendor recognition the personal brand's foundation.
